### 3. `run-analytics.sh`'s exit map still says `recorded 0 session(s)` means only regenerated bytes changed

**File:** `cli/templates/scripts/run-analytics.sh` (the header's `Exit map`) — "(n is 0 when only\n#      regenerated bytes changed)"; and its byte-identical self-adopted copy `scripts/run-analytics.sh`, at the same text

This branch adds a third reason for a write. When a new gate-log entry is the only new thing (`n` and `m` are `0`, `g` is above `0`), the script appends the entry, writes `schema: 3` and prints `recorded 0 session(s) for <branch>`. The new case "a running round log is not scanned until a later call finds its verdict" in `cli/test/run-analytics-network.test.mjs` asserts exactly that line. But the header's exit map, which the header calls the format of record for stdout (and `docs/watcher.md` → `### Run analytics` defers to it), still says `n is 0 when only regenerated bytes changed`. A new gate-log entry is an appended record, not a regenerated byte. So an operator reading `recorded 0 session(s)` in the run's log concludes that nothing new was recorded, when a gate-log entry was.

**Fix:** in both files, replace this header text:

```
#   0  stdout: `recorded <n> session(s) for <branch>` (n is 0 when only
#      regenerated bytes changed), `recorded <n> session(s) and <m> round(s)
```

with:

```
#   0  stdout: `recorded <n> session(s) for <branch>` (n is 0 when only
#      regenerated bytes or new gate-log entries changed the record, which
#      this line does not count), `recorded <n> session(s) and <m> round(s)
```

Make the edit byte-identically in `cli/templates/scripts/run-analytics.sh` and `scripts/run-analytics.sh`, so the self-adopted copy stays at the template's bytes, as Task 6 left it. The change is to a comment only and asks for no test run.
